summary: Magentic-UI combines browser interaction, code execution, file operations, and MCP tools in an interface for human-agent collaboration. name: CoAct-1: Computer-using Multi-Agent System with Coding Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CoAct-1 delegates subtasks between a GUI operator and a programmer that executes Python or Bash. Its OSWorld evaluation studies a hybrid action space in which scripts handle suitable file and data operations while visual interaction handles other steps.

name: ComputerRL: Scaling End-to-End Online Reinforcement Learning for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Combines API and GUI actions with distributed desktop reinforcement learning and alternating supervised training to address training instability.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UI-TARS-2 combines scalable trajectory generation, stabilized multi-turn reinforcement learning, and a sandbox that supports GUI, filesystem, and terminal actions. The report evaluates the resulting agent across web, desktop, Android, and game tasks and analyzes training stability.

name: MAS-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Shortcut-Augmented Hybrid Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MAS-Bench evaluates mobile agents that combine GUI actions with APIs, deep links, and reusable scripts. Its 139 tasks across 11 apps test use of 88 predefined shortcuts as well as the ability to generate new reusable workflows.

name: Secure and Efficient Access Control for Computer-Use Agents via Context Space
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CSAgent, which combines static access policies with user intent and context and enforces them through an operating-system service. A supporting toolchain constructs and refines policies for agents using API, CLI and GUI interfaces.

name: Ferret-UI Lite: Lessons from Building Small On-Device GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Ferret-UI Lite develops a 3B GUI agent using mixed real and synthetic data, reasoning with visual tools at inference, and reinforcement learning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across mobile, web, and desktop settings, including AndroidWorld and OSWorld.

name: WALT: Web Agents that Learn Tools
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WALT explores website functionality and converts demonstrated interactions into validated, reusable tools combining DOM actions, URL navigation, and agentic fallbacks. It evaluates this expanded browser action space on WebArena and VisualWebArena.

name: \textsc{GUI-Spotlight}: Adaptive Iterative Focus Refinement for Enhanced GUI Visual Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUI-Spotlight trains a grounding model to reason over images and call tools that iteratively narrow its visual focus. The paper evaluates this refinement method on ScreenSpot-Pro after training on 18,500 samples.

name: From Imperative to Declarative: Towards LLM-friendly OS Interfaces for Boosted Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a Declarative Model Interface that maps existing GUIs to access, state and observation primitives while handling low-level interactions. Evaluation uses Word, PowerPoint and Excel on Windows with a GUI-agent baseline.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UltraCUA trains a shared policy for primitive GUI actions and high-level tool calls using synthesized tasks and hybrid trajectories. Supervised fine-tuning followed by online reinforcement learning is evaluated on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.

name: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents

summary: MAI-UI combines GUI navigation, native user interaction, and MCP tool calls in a family of policies trained through generated data and online reinforcement learning. name: ComAct: Reframing Professional Software Manipulation via COM-as-Action Paradigm

name: Beyond the GUI Paradigm: Do Mobile Agents Need the Phone Screen?

name: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Describes a foundation GUI agent with combined GUI and command-line actions, large-scale interaction infrastructure, and iterative environment and task generation.

name: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: This study separates tool-adoption behavior from task competence in hybrid GUI–MCP agents. It tests tool-use incentives and screenshot-history compression, showing why changed action preferences alone need not improve held-out accuracy.

name: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents

summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.

name: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.

name: Improving Proficiency and Efficiency of Android GUI Agents via Self-Generating Tool Actions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: DroidTool generates application-state tools through proposal, implementation, testing and repair. Relational tests connect the tools’ preconditions and effects, and the resulting tools are evaluated as additions to Android GUI agents.

name: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AutoTailor compiles web trajectories into reusable browser-automation APIs, then filters and dynamically revises the capability inventory. WebArena experiments distinguish API-only operation from an agent that can fall back to ordinary reasoning and browser actions.

name: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: RecreationWorld gives hybrid agents running reference applications to explore and recreate using native GUI controls and coding tools. Its multi-platform benchmark checks interaction-dependent behavior with programmatic and visual assertions, while trajectory-training transfer is evaluated separately.

name: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MintAct trains a visual-agent family for grounding, navigation and tool use across mobile, desktop and web environments. Its shared infrastructure supports trajectory collection and asynchronous online RL while controlling cross-domain sampling and off-policy drift.

name: From Tapping to Hopping: Augmenting Mobile GUI Agents with App-Native Deeplinks
notes: Reviewed the complete retained Atom abstract and selected exact-v1 full text. The Atom has incomplete clauses; its text/hash remain unchanged and this annotation uses the explicit methods. Evaluation is Android-only, with a selected real-app subset. Landing-Activity verification is not task completion. Model/catalog release is prospective in the paper. No independent reproduction.
summary: GUI-Hopper combines verified Android deeplinks with GUI actions, using landing-screen descriptions, hybrid trajectory training and reinforcement learning to select navigation shortcuts and recover through GUI control.

name: CUA-SWE: When Computer-Use Agents Meet Visual Software Engineering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CUA-SWE, a benchmark and execution environment that combines code changes with graphical interaction and visual inspection of running software. Task-specific tests verify repairs and changes whose required information may be available only through the application interface.

name: SCOUT: Synergizing Reasoning and Tool-Use for Computer-Use Safety
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces SCOUT, a safety verifier that first derives task-specific completion and safety rubrics from a computer-use trajectory, then actively probes the resulting environment for evidence. It evaluates whether these two stages detect harmful consequences that screenshots alone can miss.

name: HybridCUA: Learning to Orchestrate GUI and CLI for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains computer agents on verified GUI, command-line, and interleaved trajectories to learn when and how to combine interaction modes.

name: CUAWright: A Minimal Unified Interface for Digital Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies a minimal terminal-based execution framework that lets digital agents construct tools and manage context across browser, desktop, and CAD tasks.

name: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Web$hell, an interface that compiles live pages into persistent information and action objects so agents can gather evidence, navigate websites, and reuse acquired content through shared operations.

name: OpenMobile-2: Building Versatile Mobile Agents with Scalable Environments and App-Native Tools
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.

name: From Observations to Authorized Actions: Measuring Source Information in Android Agents
notes: The two prototypes use different workloads and trust assumptions on patched Android/WebView components. Approval is simulated; authenticated browser delivery and atomic capture remain unimplemented. Coarse source history can withhold benign work and persist across tasks. Direct-call checks and limited live-agent trials are separate, and writes are in-memory. No production vulnerability, general defense rate or released artifact is established.
summary: Measures source-attribution limits in Android accessibility and separately tests application-history and selected-WebView-object checks for authorizing AppFunctions actions.

name: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract; experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces an open generalist computer-use stack combining visual and programmatic interaction, with model-controlled observation and task-state decisions.

name: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract; experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains native computer-use models to coordinate GUI actions and code execution using hybrid demonstrations and online reinforcement learning.

name: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
notes: The evaluated agents use Linux shell/Python/MCP tools and can inspect viewport screenshots; graphical CUA control and Windows/macOS are future work. Each agent is run once per task, with different Codex/Claude Code harnesses across systems. Scores combine weighted rubric satisfaction and model-rated visual quality. Tool counts include unsuccessful calls and do not establish matched compute or successful actions. No independent reproduction or artifact-release verification.
summary: Benchmarks agents creating editable Blender projects through shell, Python and MCP tools, judging delivered scenes with multi-view renders, task-specific rubrics and visual-quality ratings.

name: CUA-Lite: An Open Platform for Computer Use Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete official abstract and selected v1 methods, training and limitations sections. WebVoyager uses offline mirrors; VM-free sandboxes are Linux-only, and reported desktop/mobile gains do not establish unseen-app transfer. No results or released artifacts were independently reproduced.
summary: CUA-Lite unifies environment interfaces, supervised data formats and per-model harnesses for evaluation, reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning across desktop, browser and mobile tasks.

name: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 synthesis, training and evaluation sections. The system uses hybrid GUI/MCP/CLI interfaces. Evaluation includes benchmark subsets and model-based judgments, so reported scores are not treated as directly comparable GUI-only results. No independent reproduction.
summary: WildAWM synthesizes resettable GUI/MCP/CLI environments and cross-interface tasks, using execution-based checks of solvability, difficulty and verifier consistency before supervised and reinforcement learning.
